summary: Verified 3 new features: Profile Avatars, Table Photos (optional), Menu Showcase with homepage toggle. Backend: 43/43 pytest tests pass (added 13 new tests covering /api/auth/me picture field, /api/tables/public, /api/menu public+admin, owner-only menu CRUD, admin-403 on menu writes, admin-403 on /api/admin/upload, owner upload+fetch round-trip, menu_enabled toggle, table without image). Frontend: All acceptance criteria met on the live REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — landing page renders 8 'Our tables' cards (styled placeholders) and 6 'From our kitchen' menu cards publicly (no login). After customer login (guest@komorebi.cafe/Guest@123), Navbar shows initials Avatar ('AT') next to logout button which shows first name 'Aiko'. /reservations page shows full name 'Aiko Tanaka' with avatar/initials. As Super Admin, Owner console → Owner settings tab exposes 'Menu showcase' panel with all required testids (add-menu-btn, menu-name, menu-description, menu-price, menu-category, menu-image-upload, save-menu-btn) — successfully created a menu item via UI and saw success toast + list update. setting-menu-enabled and save-settings-btn present. Tables & Status tab → Add table dialog has optional table-image-upload as required. Menu toggle round-trip verified via API (enabled=false hides menu, restored to true). Owner upload endpoint returns /api/files/<path> and serves image with 200 + image content-type. Made one small fix in server.py to guarantee /auth/me always returns a 'picture' field (was missing for pre-existing seeded users).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /auth/me was returning the raw user document, which omitted 'picture' for users seeded before the field was added. Fixed by adding user.setdefault('picture', '') in get_current_user. Consider adding a one-time migration to backfill 'picture' on all existing users for schema consistency.

server.py: MenuItemInput uses price:int — good, matches ₹ integer usage. However update_menu overwrites created_at loss risk? Actually update_menu uses body.model_dump() which does NOT include created_at (not in model), so $set only writes body fields — safe.

server.py: /api/admin/upload rejects non-image extensions but does not validate actual file magic bytes; a caller can send an .png named file with arbitrary content up to 8MB. Low risk since endpoint is owner-only, but consider magic-byte validation.

frontend Landing.js: 'Our tables' and 'From our kitchen' sections use conditional render on length>0 and enabled — behaves correctly. Image url handling supports both absolute (http) and /api/files/ relative — resolved via BACKEND prefix. Good.
frontend server.py line count is now 951 — approaching the 700-line refactor guideline. Consider splitting routers (auth/reservations/admin/media/menu) into modules.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all new-feature checks + navbar avatar + MyReservations header + owner menu CRUD via UI + table image upload field + landing sections public)
